name: Tom mu ni
summary: Slipper lobster, boiled, with the meat in the tail. Vietnam National Authority of Tourism says it is clawless, and the dip is lime, salt, and Phú Quốc pepper. It is served in upmarket restaurants and at the night market. A door was not named. A price is Check on arrival.
origin: Phu Quoc, on the specialty-seafood account.
texture: White meat. The specialty-seafood account says the texture sits between shrimp and lobster.
taste: Sweeter than other lobster, on that account. The dip is lime, salt, and Phú Quốc pepper. The meat is boiled until tender and aromatic.
howToEat: Eat the tail, dipped in lime, salt, and pepper.
Upmarket restaurants and the night market. No door was named. An hour and a price are Check on arrival.
where: Upmarket restaurants and the night market. A door is Check on arrival.
